accuracy.evidence: Matched to the KS1 working scientifically statements in the DfE science programme of study (performing simple tests; observing closely, using simple equipment; using observations and ideas to suggest answers to questions; gathering and recording data) and to the topic's three evidence lines (one thing changing at a time, observe and describe, use the result to answer the question). The adult text says fair testing proper is a lower-KS2 (Years 3 and 4) statement, which is where the programme of study puts 'comparative and fair tests'. Science checked: absorbent kitchen towel wicks water further than facial tissue and much further than coated shiny paper (capillary action through cellulose fibres; the 9 / 6 / 1 squares are presented as one test's results, not a constant); ice in direct sun melts faster than identical ice in shade, and a smaller cube melts sooner, which is why sizes must match.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common KS1 and early KS2 enquiry slips: changing two variables at once (unfair-kit step, m6 chair-versus-table drop, challenge tag 'two'), 'fixing' the variable under test (the 'Make the papers the same' decoy button and challenge tag 'none'), holding on to a prediction against the result (step 4 prediction, p4, challenge tag 'guess'), reporting what was expected rather than what was seen (p5, tag 'look') and treating a wrong prediction as failure (m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsimtest is built on running a test: strips that only show their water height after being dipped, a setup whose three unfair differences (water level, strip width, timer) are each fixed by tapping while the paper must stay different, a squares count that fills a results table, an answer picked from that table, and an ice test that will not start until the cubes match. flagsciq sorts kinds of questions, flaghlens is a hand lens, flagramp is slopes and rolling; the shingle gate is under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child guesses, then the canvas shows the water climbing 9, 6 and 1 squares before any text names a winner; the unfair kit flags each difference with a red mark that clears only when it is fixed; the table is built from the child's own counts and is the only thing on screen when the question is answered; the ice cubes melt only after the test is fair. The step text then confirms the rule (change one thing, look, record, answer from results).

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option: 'Shiny paper, it looks strong' (judging by look not test), 'Yes, it is still a test' for unequal times, 'Keep her guess' after a contrary result, 'Nothing else' for the ice test (forgetting cube size) and 'Both at the same time' for sun versus shade. Each is then contradicted or confirmed by what the canvas shows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge items, each with two tagged wrong answers (two, none, guess, cannot, look); every message names the slip, e.g. 'Two things are changing. Change only one thing, or you cannot tell which one made the difference.' and 'A guess is not the answer. The result of the test is the answer.' Wrong taps in the lab also name the slip ('Square 7 is still dry. Look where the dark colour stops.').

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences and concrete words (paper, water, squares, guess, same, change); 'fair test' is introduced once with its meaning. Adult text keeps sentences short and passes validate_lessons (family limits) first time; curriculum terms used precisely: simple test, prediction, observe, record, results, fair test.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean; each kid paragraph carries one stage of a test (ask and guess, change one thing, look and record, answer from results) and each lab step practises one of the topic's three evidence lines.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android light and iPhone 13 dark screenshots after Show me on every step. The first pass squashed long messages and the challenge question into one compressed line and clipped the strip labels in the count step; both were fixed (text now wraps onto lines; the count step no longer shifts the strips up). Young mode gives 56 px buttons for every action, and the strips and cups are large tap targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas tap has a button twin (Dip each paper, Fix the water / strip size / time, three count buttons, three paper choices, Make the ice the same size, Start the test, Wait 10 minutes); the canvas aria-label is rewritten with every result and challenge question; walk.cjs reports axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
